extraction.name: BoolQ
extraction.description: A reading comprehension dataset of 16,000 naturally occurring yes/no questions paired with Wikipedia paragraphs. The questions are generated in unprompted and unconstrained settings, often query for complex, non-factoid information, and require difficult entailment-like inference to solve.
extraction.creator: Christopher Clark, Kenton Lee, Ming-Wei Chang, Tom Kwiatkowski, Michael Collins, Kristina Toutanova
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset consists of questions, paragraphs from Wikipedia articles, article titles, and yes/no answers. Questions were gathered to construct a dedicated yes/no QA dataset, building upon Natural Questions which contained too few natural yes/no questions (about 1% of the corpus).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Wikipedia articles and questions from Natural Questions corpus, with paragraphs extracted from Wikipedia articles paired with yes/no questions and answers.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Passages that present more straightforward factual information (like Wikipedia introduction paragraphs) correlate with 'yes' answers. There is little signal in the question by itself, but some language patterns in the passage correlate with the answer.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset contains unexpectedly challenging questions that often query for complex, non-factoid information and require difficult entailment-like inference to solve. There is a significant performance gap between the best model (80.4% accuracy) and human annotators (90% accuracy).
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for yes/no question answering tasks, with examples used for training, development, and testing. It can be used for transfer learning experiments and fine-tuning pre-trained language models.

name.evidence: We follow the data collection method used by Natural Questions (NQ) (Kwiatkowski et al., 2019) to gather 16,000 naturally occurring yes/no questions into a dataset we call BoolQ (for Boolean Questions).

description.evidence: We build a reading comprehension dataset, BoolQ, of such questions, and show that they are unexpectedly challenging. They often query for complex, non-factoid information, and require difficult entailment-like inference to solve.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: An example in our dataset consists of a question, a paragraph from a Wikipedia article, the title of the article, and an answer, which is either 'yes' or 'no'... This work builds upon the Natural Questions (NQ) (Kwiatkowski et al., 2019), which contains some natural yes/no questions. However, there are too few (about 1% of the corpus) to make yes/no QA a very important aspect of that task. In this paper, we gather a large number of additional yes/no questions in order to construct a dedicated yes/no QA dataset.
